recommendations.title: Review recent high-severity anomalies
recommendations.explanation: 1 high-severity anomaly event(s) in the last 30 days. Most severe: unusually low use around Sun 2009-12-13 01:00: 0.36 kW vs typical 1.12 kW for this hour of the week, 2.9x the edge of the usual range for this hour (the 99.5th-percentile deviation of the last 26 weeks). Event spans 3 h.
caveats: An anomaly is an unusual reading, not a confirmed fault; unusual-but-legitimate use (guests, holidays) is flagged too.

recommendations.title: Check always-on devices
recommendations.explanation: Your lowest sustained demand is about 0.30 kW (the 5th percentile of hourly use), about 24% of all energy. Fridges and routers account for part of it; old appliances, standby electronics and heating elements are common extras.
caveats: Figures are scenario estimates under the stated assumption, not forecasts of savings.
The tariff in use is the built-in DEMO tariff; replace it with your real rates before relying on any cost figure.
The 'baseload' is a statistical floor of the whole-house reading, not a measurement of individual devices.

recommendations.title: High demand expected in the next 24 hours
recommendations.explanation: The forecast peaks at 2.68 kW around Fri 20:00, higher than 92% of the hours in your last 90 days and inside the most expensive tariff period. Staggering heavy appliances around that time lowers the peak.
caveats: This is a model forecast with its own error; see the model page for the measured accuracy at this horizon.

recommendations.title: Move flexible use out of the most expensive hours
recommendations.explanation: 18% of your energy in the last 90 days was used in the most expensive tariff hours (17:00-21:00), which are only 12% of the hours. Running dishwashers, washing machines or EV charging outside those hours is the simplest saving.

scenario.assumption: 10% of the dearest-period energy is moved to the cheapest hours

caveats: Figures are scenario estimates under the stated assumption, not forecasts of savings.
The tariff in use is the built-in DEMO tariff; replace it with your real rates before relying on any cost figure.
Only flexible loads (laundry, dishwasher, EV charging, water heating) can usually be moved.
